topic: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (004) certification exam preparation - infrastructure as code with Terraform, Terraform fundamentals and providers, the core init/plan/apply/destroy workflow, writing HCL configuration, modules, state management and remote backends, maintaining infrastructure, and HCP Terraform (Terraform Cloud)
exam_format: Approximately 57 questions, 60 minutes, delivered online with remote proctoring via Certiverse (requires a compliant system, webcam, and stable internet). Question types are multiple choice, multiple response, true/false, fill-in-the-blank, and text-match. Provider-specific cloud knowledge is NOT required - the exam is provider-agnostic and focuses on Terraform itself. HashiCorp does not publish a fixed passing percentage; present the pass threshold as unpublished. The certification is valid for two years. Exam fee is approximately USD 70.50 plus applicable taxes and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current HashiCorp pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE', plus true/false and fill-in-the-blank style items reframed as 4-option questions for the practice bank; questions test Terraform behavior, HCL syntax, command output, and 'which approach is correct' judgment - NOT cloud-provider trivia
audience: Cloud engineers, DevOps engineers, platform and SRE practitioners, and infrastructure developers who use or want to use Terraform to manage infrastructure as code across any cloud. This is a foundational/associate credential - no deep prior Terraform experience is required, though basic familiarity with the command line and cloud concepts helps. HashiCorp positions it as the entry point to the Terraform certification path. A strong DevOps/IaC complement to the cloud-architecture and cloud-engineer courses (Google Associate Cloud Engineer, Professional Cloud Architect, AWS SAA) already in this catalog, and the first HashiCorp course in the catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Understand infrastructure as code (IaC) concepts
domains.notes: What IaC is and the problems it solves; the advantages of IaC patterns (versioning, repeatability, automation, collaboration, drift reduction); and how Terraform enables multi-cloud, hybrid-cloud, and provider-agnostic workflows. Foundational 'why Terraform' framing that later chapters build on. Choosing the IaC benefit or concept that matches a described situation.

domains.name: Understand Terraform's purpose (vs other IaC)
domains.notes: How Terraform compares to and complements other IaC and configuration tools; Terraform's declarative model, execution plan, resource graph, and provider ecosystem; where Terraform fits alongside tools like Ansible, and the value of state-driven provisioning. Explaining why a Terraform approach fits a described automation goal.

domains.name: Terraform fundamentals: providers and state basics
domains.notes: Installing and versioning providers; the required_providers/provider blocks, the dependency lock file (.terraform.lock.hcl), and provider version constraints; how Terraform uses plugins/providers to talk to APIs; writing configuration that uses multiple providers and provider aliases; and a first understanding of how Terraform uses and manages state to map configuration to real resources. Picking the correct provider/version-pinning or state concept for a scenario.

domains.name: The core Terraform workflow (Write, Plan, Apply)
domains.notes: The everyday workflow and CLI commands: terraform init (backend + provider setup), validate, plan (generate and review an execution plan), apply (create/update infrastructure), destroy, and fmt (formatting/style). Reading plan output, understanding what changes Terraform proposes and why, and the resource graph behind it. Choosing the right command or interpreting command output for a described task.

domains.name: Write and maintain Terraform configuration (HCL)
domains.notes: Authoring HCL: differentiating resource vs data blocks; referencing resource attributes and building cross-resource references and dependencies (implicit and explicit depends_on); input variables and outputs; complex types (list, set, map, object, tuple); dynamic configuration with expressions, built-in functions, for/for_each and count, and dynamic blocks; validating configuration with custom conditions (variable validation, preconditions/postconditions, checks); and best practices for sensitive data, including marking values sensitive and integrating with HashiCorp Vault. Choosing the correct HCL construct for a described requirement.

domains.name: Interact with Terraform modules
domains.notes: How Terraform sources modules (local paths, the public/private Registry, Git, versioned sources); variable scope and passing values into modules; using module outputs and composing modules; and managing module versions with the version argument. Choosing the right module source, input/output wiring, or version constraint for a described reuse scenario.

domains.name: Manage Terraform state and remote backends
domains.notes: How state works and why it exists; the local backend; state locking and why it matters for teams; configuring remote state with the backend block (and awareness of common remote backends); managing resource drift and refactoring state with terraform state commands, refresh-only mode, and the moved and removed blocks; importing behavior and inspecting state. Choosing the correct state/backend/drift approach for a described situation, including sensitive-data-in-state considerations.

domains.name: Understand HCP Terraform (Terraform Cloud) capabilities
domains.notes: Using HCP Terraform (formerly Terraform Cloud) to provision infrastructure: workspaces and projects, remote operations and remote state, and the CLI-driven/VCS-driven/API-driven run workflows; collaboration and governance features (private module registry, variable sets, policy enforcement with Sentinel/OPA, run triggers, drift detection, dynamic provider credentials, teams and RBAC); and how the cloud/HCP integration differs from Community Edition. Choosing the correct HCP Terraform feature for a described collaboration or governance need.

extra_guidance: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (004) is the leading Infrastructure-as-Code credential and a top DevOps cert with broad, cross-cloud demand and a low ~USD 70.50 exam fee that drives high conversion. This is the FIRST HashiCorp course in the catalog and expands the brand from pure AI/cloud-vendor certs into DevOps/IaC. VERSION: build the CURRENT 004 exam - the 003 version RETIRED on January 8, 2026. State clearly that 003 is retired and this course targets 004; note that 004 added deeper coverage of custom conditions/checks, the moved/removed blocks, refresh-only drift handling, and refreshed HCP Terraform governance features, and reflects the HCP Terraform (formerly 'Terraform Cloud') rename. The exam is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC: HashiCorp explicitly says provider-specific cloud knowledge is NOT required, so teach Terraform itself and, when examples need a provider, keep them generic/illustrative rather than AWS/Azure/GCP-specific deep dives. This course DOES involve reading and writing HCL at a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND level - show and explain real HCL snippets and terraform command output (init/plan/apply/destroy/fmt/validate/state/import), variables/outputs, for_each vs count, modules, backend blocks, moved/removed blocks - rather than requiring students to run a live cloud account; make that explicit. Use EXACT current terminology: HCL, provider, required_providers, the dependency lock file (.terraform.lock.hcl), resource vs data blocks, state and remote backends, state locking, drift, terraform import, modules and the Terraform Registry, workspaces, and HCP Terraform (workspaces, projects, private registry, variable sets, Sentinel/OPA policy, run triggers, dynamic credentials) - with a one-line note that Terraform evolves fast (and 'Terraform Cloud' is now 'HCP Terraform'), so verify against current docs. The EIGHT domain names above are HashiCorp's official 004 objective areas; the percentage weights are APPROXIMATE editorial estimates (HashiCorp does not publish per-objective weights) - say so where weights appear. Practice questions should mirror the exam's mix: 'which command', interpreting plan/state output, correct HCL construct, module sourcing/versioning, state/backend/locking/drift decisions, sensitive-data handling, and HCP Terraform feature selection - plus reframed true/false and fill-in-the-blank items as 4-option questions. Cover classic traps: count vs for_each, implicit vs explicit dependencies (depends_on), terraform plan vs apply refresh behavior, local vs remote state and locking, moved vs removed vs state rm, terraform import limits, provider version pinning and the lock file, and Community Edition vs HCP Terraform capabilities. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 70.50 plus tax, varies by region), note the two-year validity and online Certiverse proctoring, and advise verifying current HashiCorp pricing and the latest exam objectives. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 60-minute time-management strategy for ~57 questions. Scan the practice bank for stray cloud-vendor-specific or other-vendor terms before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
